subject: mathematics
question_text: If A is the matrix with rows (−1, −2, −2), (2, 1, −2) and (2, −2, 1), then show that adj A = 3Aᵀ, and also find A⁻¹.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

steps.label: Find det A
steps.margin_note: First mark. Expand along the top row. It comes to 27, which is 3³ — a hint that the factor of 3 in the question is not accidental.
steps.memory_tip: det A = 27, which is 3³ — a hint that the 3 in the question is not accidental.

accept: expand the determinant to get twenty seven
det A is twenty seven
the determinant comes to twenty seven
determinant twenty seven vasthundi
compute the determinant first

steps.why: 27 is 3³, and the 3 in adj A = 3Aᵀ is the same 3. Noticing that early makes the rest feel less arbitrary.
common_mistakes: Sign slip on the middle term.
Expanding along a row with no zeros unnecessarily.

steps.label: Find the adjoint
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Nine cofactors, then transpose. The cofactor matrix is not symmetric here, so skipping the transpose gives the wrong matrix.
steps.memory_tip: Nine cofactors, then transpose. The cofactor matrix is not symmetric here, so the transpose really does change it.

recall.must_convey: That the adjoint is computed as the transposed cofactor matrix.
accept: find the nine cofactors and transpose to get the adjoint
the adjoint is the transposed cofactor matrix
compute adj A
cofactors teeskoni transpose cheyyali
build the adjoint

steps.why: Every entry of the adjoint is a multiple of 3, which is the first visible sign that the claimed identity will hold.
common_mistakes: Losing a sign in the cofactor board.

steps.label: Compute 3Aᵀ and compare
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Transpose A, multiply every entry by 3, and set it beside the adjoint — the claim is an equality, so both sides must be shown.
steps.memory_tip: The claim is an EQUALITY, so both sides must be written out and set side by side.

recall.must_convey: That 3Aᵀ is computed and shown to be identical to the adjoint.
accept: transpose A and multiply by three then compare with the adjoint, they match
three A transpose equals the adjoint
both sides are the same matrix
three A transpose adjoint tho same
compare the two matrices

steps.why: Showing two matrices are equal means displaying both. Computing only one and asserting the match is not a proof.

steps.label: Find A⁻¹
steps.margin_note: Last mark. A⁻¹ = (Adj A)/det A = 3Aᵀ/27 = Aᵀ/9 — the identity just proved makes this one line instead of nine.
steps.memory_tip: A⁻¹ = 3Aᵀ/27 = Aᵀ/9 — the identity just proved makes this one line instead of nine.

accept: A inverse is the adjoint over twenty seven which is three A transpose over twenty seven equals A transpose over nine
use the identity just proved to shortcut the inverse
the answer is one ninth of A transpose
adjoint by twenty seven, ante A transpose by nine
the inverse is one over nine times A transpose

steps.why: The first part of the question was set up to make the second part immediate. Using it rather than starting again is what the two parts are for.
common_mistakes: Recomputing the adjoint for the inverse.

insider_note: det A = 27 = 3³, which is why the adjoint comes out as exactly 3Aᵀ. Once that is shown, A⁻¹ = 3Aᵀ/27 = Aᵀ/9 with no further cofactor work.
